entities.name: Edward Neville, 3rd Baron Bergavenny
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Edward Neville, 3rd Baron Bergavenny (1434-1476) was a prominent English nobleman who played a crucial role in the medieval politics of the realm. As a key figure in the Wars of the Roses, he fought alongside Richard, Duke of York, and later supported the Lancastrian claimant, Henry VI. His significance lies in his ability to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the rival houses, ultimately contributing to the downfall of the Plantagenet dynasty.




The 3rd Baron Bergavenny's legacy can be seen in the many land grants and titles he held, including the barony of Bergavenny in Shropshire. His influence extended beyond the nobility, as he was also a patron of the arts, supporting local churches and monasteries.




A poignant reminder of his enduring impact is the Neville family's continued presence in English politics for centuries to come, with his descendant, Richard Neville, 16th Baron Bergavenny, playing a key role in the reign of King Henry VIII.




This landmark 1476 event marked the beginning of a new era in English history, one that would be shaped by the complex interplay of power, family, and loyalty that characterized the medieval period.
